event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, dated less than one year after the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic, presents COVID-19 as an ongoing and multifaceted risk to Avery Dennison (AVY).  Management discloses both realized impacts (2020 revenue declines, a quantified 15 % sales drop in Q2, credit-market disruption, manufacturing shutdowns and a 65 % jump in credit-loss reserves) and forward-looking uncertainties (supply-chain fragility, labor availability, remote-work resilience, liquidity access, macro-economic downturn and cost re-inflation).  While the narrative notes some sequential improvement and temporary cost savings, these are framed as partial and potentially reversible mitigation measures.  Because the pandemic’s effects are contemporaneous with the 2021 filing and many statements describe material, already-incurred losses as well as credible future exposure, the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores (up to 10).  Individual sentence scores therefore reflect: (1) directness and specificity of the linkage to COVID-19, (2) presence of quantification or “material adverse” language, (3) breadth of impact (operations, supply chain, finance, workforce, demand), and (4) any explicit mitigating factors that moderate—though do not eliminate—the risk.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 has had an adverse effect on portions of our business and we could experience further negative consequences as a result of COVID-19 that could have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Acknowledges direct past impact (‘has had an adverse effect’).
Projects additional future material adverse consequences.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, already-realized harm plus explicit warning of further material damage yields a high recent-event risk score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Overall, the pandemic had a negative impact on our consolidated financial results for 2020.

components.reason: States an enterprise-wide negative financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirms broad financial harm but without quantification, meriting a solid mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: While we experienced sequential improvements in the second half of 2020, net sales for the full year were lower across our reportable segments due to the continued negative impact of the pandemic.

components.reason: Reports continuing pandemic-driven sales decline.
Mentions sequential improvement, a mitigating factor.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Negative impact tempered by partial recovery lowers the severity to 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Net sales for the second quarter of 2020 were down approximately 15% from the same period in 2019.

components.reason: Quantifies a significant pandemic-period revenue drop (15 %).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: A concrete, sizeable figure supports a strong score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We are unable to predict the full impact that COVID-19 will have on our 2021 results from operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows due to numerous uncertainties, including the duration and severity of the pandemic and containment measures and the related macroeconomic impacts.

components.reason: Highlights significant unpredictability of future financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking uncertainty elevates risk but absence of quantification keeps it moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: The ability of our employees to work has been and may continue to be significantly impacted by COVID-19.

components.reason: Identifies workforce disruption as an ongoing operational risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational continuity threat yields a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our office and management personnel in certain countries have generally worked from home since mid-March 2020, and some of our employees engaged in manufacturing, production and distribution facilities were at times restricted by governmental orders from coming to work.

components.reason: Details remote-work shift and production staffing restrictions.
Indicates continuation of operations via remote work (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes real disruptions but also partial mitigation, resulting in a score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced, and may experience in the future, temporary facility closures in response to government mandates in certain jurisdictions in which we operate.

components.reason: Confirms facility shutdowns already occurred.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Actual shutdowns represent direct operational risk, scoring 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Delays in production or delivery of components or raw materials in our global supply chain, or the ability to transport those components or materials or our finished goods, due to restrictions imposed to limit the spread of COVID-19 could delay or inhibit our ability to obtain supply of components and materials to deliver finished goods to customers.

components.reason: Highlights potential supply-chain bottlenecks tied to pandemic restrictions.
Impact remains prospective rather than realized.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Significant but still conditional supply-chain threat scores 3.

evidence_list.snippet: While disruptions to our supply chain during fiscal year 2020 were not significant, if conditions worsen or last for an extended period of time, our supply chains could be materially adversely affected.

components.reason: Forecasts possible material adverse supply-chain impact.
States past disruptions were not significant (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Risk exists but is presently limited, yielding a low score of 1.

evidence_list.snippet: In the first quarter of 2020, our ability to access the commercial paper market was disrupted and we drew down $500 million from our revolving credit facility, which we repaid in the second quarter of 2020.

components.reason: Documents an actual liquidity shock and $500 million drawdown.
Repayment indicates partial resolution (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Quantified liquidity stress offset by quick repayment results in a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: Macroeconomic developments such as impacts from COVID-19, slower growth in the geographic regions in which we operate, the restructuring of European sovereign and other debt obligations, the impact of the exit of the United Kingdom (“UK”) from the European Union (commonly known as “Brexit”), and uncertainty in the global credit or financial markets leading to a loss of consumer confidence could result in a material adverse effect on our business as a result of, among other things, reduced consumer spending, declines in asset valuations, diminished liquidity and credit availability, volatility in securities prices, credit rating downgrades, and fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates.

components.reason: Links COVID-19 to broad macroeconomic and consumer-demand risks.
COVID-19 is mixed with other generic factors, diluting specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generalized macro risk attribution produces a modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: In early 2020, in response to the initial outbreak of COVID-19, many of our manufacturing and other operations in China experienced limited production and/or closure; as the outbreak spread beyond this region, our facilities in other countries were similarly impacted, most significantly in South Asia.

components.reason: Cites actual production limits and closures across multiple regions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Geographically widespread shutdowns warrant a high operational-risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: All of our manufacturing facilities are currently open, but, many of our employees are still unable to travel within and outside their countries.

components.reason: Travel restrictions hamper operations and logistics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Ongoing mobility limits present moderate risk (score 2).

evidence_list.snippet: There could be disruptions in our supply chain or ability to manufacture our products, as well as temporary closures of our facilities or those of our suppliers or customers, any of which could impact our sales and operating results.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple pandemic-driven operational disruption scenarios.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad potential operational impacts merit a mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 has adversely affected the economies and financial markets in impacted countries, and further escalation of the health crisis could potentially lead to a more significant economic downturn that could adversely affect demand for our products and negatively impact our business.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to macro downturn and product-demand risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Material market-demand risk yields a strong score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 adversely impacted our results for fiscal year 2020; while we took measures to mitigate this impact, they were unable to fully offset it.

components.reason: Confirms adverse financial results.
Mitigation measures only partially effective.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Partial mitigation keeps the risk elevated at 3.

evidence_list.snippet: As our business environment changes, including as a result of COVID-19, we have adjusted and may need to further adjust our business strategies or restructure our operations or particular businesses.

components.reason: Indicates strategic and restructuring responses required by pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Need for ongoing strategic adjustment shows moderate exposure.

evidence_list.snippet: We have also reduced costs across our company in response to COVID-19, approximately $135 million of which we believe to be temporary, meaning that we anticipate the majority of these costs to return as markets recover.

components.reason: Temporary cost actions highlight future cost rebound risk.
Cost reductions currently provide mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Temporary nature of savings implies limited long-term mitigation, but immediate risk is low (score 1).

evidence_list.snippet: Although we have processes to administer credit granted to customers and believe our allowance for credit losses is adequate, we have experienced losses – including an approximately 65% increase in our allowance for credit losses from approximately $27 million to approximately $45 million in the 2020 as a result of COVID-19 – and in the future may experience losses as a result of our inability to collect some of our accounts receivable.

components.reason: Quantifies a 65 % spike in credit-loss reserves attributable to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Large, quantified hit to credit quality justifies a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: In March 2020, we paused our share repurchase activity in response to COVID-19 after buying approximately $45 million of our stock in the quarter.

components.reason: Shows capital-allocation restraint due to pandemic uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Signal of caution, but limited operational impact, scores 2.

evidence_list.snippet: If our access to commercial paper markets were to become limited, as they were in March 2020 as a result of COVID-19, and we were required to obtain short-term funding under our revolving credit facility or our other credit facilities, we would face increased exposure to variable interest rates.

components.reason: Identifies specific financing risk recurring from prior COVID-19 disruption.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential recurrence of funding stress merits a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: If these conditions worsen, or last for an extended period of time, or there is a disruption in the technology we use to operate remotely, our ability to manage our business may be impaired, and operational, cybersecurity and other risks facing us prior to the pandemic may be elevated.

components.reason: Highlights compounded operational and cybersecurity risks under prolonged pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Elevated multi-risk scenario justifies a higher score.

evidence_list.snippet: We cannot predict the impact of COVID-19 on our customers, suppliers, vendors, and other business partners, including our financing sources, and how these impacts will affect our business.

components.reason: Emphasizes uncertainty regarding counterparties and overall business effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty across the value chain supports a mid-tier score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 has affected and is likely to continue affecting our customers, suppliers, vendors, and other business partners, but we are not able to predict the ultimate consequences that will result.

components.reason: Acknowledges ongoing widespread stakeholder impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Continued stakeholder disruption warrants a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: If our sales channels were to become substantially impacted for an extended period of time, our business could be materially adversely affected.

components.reason: Potential material adverse effect on revenue channels.
Conditional language indicates possibility rather than certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Conditional but serious sales-channel risk results in a score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: The pandemic and any other adverse development in emerging markets could have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Links pandemic to potential material adverse impact in key growth regions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emerging-market sensitivity yields a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which the pandemic will impact our financial results is dependent on future developments, which are uncertain and unpredictable.

components.reason: Highlights fundamental uncertainty of future financial impacts.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty over future outcomes maintains mid-level severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Some of these temporary cost reductions are expected to return in 2021, which would increase our costs, in connection with growth or other changes in our business.

components.reason: Foresees pandemic-related costs re-inflating and pressuring margins.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Cost rebound risk is real but not yet quantified, giving a score of 2.
